chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The end of the Aqeeq is Bareyd Awtaas. And he said: The Bareyd of Al-Ba's is before Ghamra by two Bareyds.

key_terms.الْعَقِيق: Aqeeq: A well-known place near Mecca, one of the Miqat stations for entering Ihraam.
key_terms.بَرِيدُ أَوْطَاس: Bareyd Awtaas: A specific location identified as the end of the Aqeeq region.
key_terms.بَرِيدُ الْبَعْث: Bareyd Al-Ba's: A location associated with the tribe of Bakr or a specific station.
key_terms.بِبَرِيدَيْنِ: By two Bareyds: A measurement of distance, where a 'Bareyd' is a traditional unit of distance.
key_terms.غَمْرَةَ: Ghamra: A place near Mecca, another Miqat station for pilgrims.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific locations for entering Ihraam at Aqeeq and Ghamra according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific miqat (juncture) for the Aqeeq region, identifying Bareyd Awtaas as its terminus and clarifying the distance of Bareyd Al-Ba's relative to Ghamra. In Shia jurisprudence, these precise geographical markers are crucial for determining the validity of Hajj rituals, as entering Ihraam before the designated point is obligatory. The narration reflects the scholarly emphasis on exactitude in ritual boundaries, ensuring pilgrims fulfill their religious duties according to the Imams' teachings.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘At the end of Al-Aqeeq is Bareyd Owtaas’. And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Bareyd of Al-Ba’as is besides Ghamra by two Bareyds’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘
The last section of al-‘Aqiq is Barid of Awtas.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Barid al-Ba‘th is two Barid before Ghamrah.””
